v1.15.0 closes the 1.14 series. Its headline is structural: a chart of accounts can now map into
more than one reporting framework. Each mapping is anchored to its own taxonomy, which records the
framework it maps into, and everything that reads a mapping picks it by framework rather than taking
the first one it finds. rs-gaap is the book framework today. Tax and full us-gaap will each be one
more mapping of the same shape. The series also adds a write-capable AI operator behind the console's
`/do`, an audit trail of every change made to a graph, and deliberate, write-safe graph writer
replacement.

Covers everything since v1.14.0; the 1.14.x patches carried generated changelogs.

## Upgrade notes

**Client SDKs 2.3.0 pair with this release.** The change is additive:
- `TaxonomyBlockStructureRequest` and `TaxonomyBlockStructure` gain an optional `target_framework`.
- The GraphQL `Structure` type gains `framework`.
- `LedgerClient.list_mappings` / `list_structures` (TypeScript: `listMappings` / `listStructures`) now return `framework`.

Those two facade calls request the new field, so **client 2.3.0 needs a server at v1.15.0 or later**. Against v1.14.x they fail GraphQL validation. Every other call is unaffected.

**Behaviour changes worth knowing:**
- **A chart holds one mapping per framework.** A second mapping into the same framework is refused (422), as is a `coa_mapping` structure on any block other than a chart of accounts. An unknown `target_framework` is a 422.
- **The mappings list puts the book mapping first** and reports each mapping's `framework`.
- **A mapping's `taxonomyId` now names its mapping taxonomy**, not the chart. A chart's structures listing (`structures(taxonomyId: <chart>)`) includes its mappings.
- **Every mapping write path refuses a computed subtotal as a target**: `create-mapping-association`, the suggester, mapping arcs written through `update-taxonomy-block`, and reporting extensions.
- **`materialize` on a ledger graph that already holds data rebuilds blue-green**, whatever `rebuild` says. It previously tried an in-place load that always failed on such a graph.
- **File operations moved rate-limit buckets.** `create-file-upload` counts against table uploads, and `ingest-file` and `delete-file` against table management, instead of graph management. A multi-table load no longer hits the graph-management limit.
- **`create-event-block` declares itself destructive to MCP clients.** With handlers applied it can post entries.

**Deploy:** from v1.14.12, one extensions migration, `0037`. It re-anchors each chart's existing mapping in every tenant schema:
- the target is the framework the mapping's arcs point into, or rs-gaap if it has none;
- a mapping stays active only if it was active;
- where a chart holds two active mappings into one framework, the one with the most arcs stays active.

Structure ids are unchanged, so reports and the graph are unaffected. From v1.14.0 there is also one platform migration, adding the mutation audit table, and a new `OPERATION_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS` setting (default 396). CloudFormation changes are in the OIDC bootstrap stack, the worker stack (a graph-write-failure alarm) and the graph infrastructure stack.

## Chart mappings, one per framework

- **Each `coa_mapping` structure hangs off a `mapping` taxonomy the chart owns.** Its source is the chart and its target is the framework's reporting taxonomy. The framework is read from the target and stored nowhere else. A unique index holds one active mapping per chart and framework.
- **The chart's taxonomy block is the chart plus the mappings it owns.** Creating, reading, updating and deleting a chart through the taxonomy-block operations behaves as before. Removing a mapped account removes its arcs, and deleting a chart deletes its mappings.
- **Readers select by framework.** That covers statements, month-end statement stamping, account rollups, the QuickBooks auto-map and the sync's mapping setup.

## AI operators

- **The author operator.** The console's `/do` can make changes, such as adding a vendor or creating a metric block, rather than only reading. A run is bounded by a 750-credit ceiling when the request sets none. It reports every write it made however it ends, including on failure, budget exhaustion or cancellation, so a retry doesn't repeat them.
- **Claude Opus 5.5.** It is registered as an operator model with effort carried to the model call, and the `quality` tier moves to it. The default `balanced` tier is unchanged. Opus 5.5 cache reads are billed at Bedrock's rate for that model.
- The first operator call after a quiet spell no longer fails on a pooled connection the network dropped while it sat idle.

## Audit trail

- **Every mutating call on a graph is recorded**, whether it came through the REST API, an MCP client or an in-app operator. Each record says which operation ran, for whom, through which credential or operator run, and what it touched. Arguments are never stored.
- Graph admins read the trail at `GET /v1/graphs/{graph_id}/audit/mutations`. Operations that finish asynchronously are included.

## Graph tier and deploys

- **Writers are replaced only when a deploy opts in.** A release whose change set would replace graph writers (a new AMI, userdata or instance type) now leaves them as they are and reports the pending roll, unless the dispatch opts in with `cycle_writers`. The rest of the release deploys normally.
- **An opted-in roll is safe for writes.** New graph writes are paused at admission with `503` + `Retry-After`. In-flight writes drain before each tier cycles. A failed graph write alerts the worker alerts inbox. The graph client follows a replaced writer on its next call.
- **Rolling container refreshes.** The refresh walks the fleet one instance at a time and returns to busy instances last. Busy state is a per-operation lease that expires by itself, and an instance still busy at the deadline gets a follow-up run rather than failing the deploy.
- A writer's startup waits out its volume attach in one attempt, and a new database is recorded only on its writer's own volume.
- Materializing a graph with a fixed-size vector column no longer crashes the Graph API.
- Multi-key `ORDER BY` queries return correct rows past a few thousand sorted rows. This works around an engine sort defect. MCP row caps apply at a query's final `RETURN`.

## Reporting and mapping

- A chart that maps one account straight to PP&E Net and others to Gross and Accumulated Depreciation renders all of them, so the balance sheet foots.
- The mapping coverage summary no longer reports negative confidence bands, and it treats PP&E Gross and Accumulated Depreciation mappings as reachable.
- Schedule facts are excluded from `build-fact-grid`, so two schedules posting to one account no longer collapse into one amount, and projections don't sort ahead of actuals.
- A re-pointed library arc replaces its predecessor in the library and in every tenant, instead of standing beside it.

## MCP

- **`get-report-bundle`** returns a short-lived link to a published report's Tavi, holon or XBRL 2.1 package, which a client can hand to any tool that loads a file by URL.
- Tool annotations are declared per tool.
- Several tool descriptions (`close-period`, `list-subgraphs`) now state facts rather than instructions, as AI-client directory reviews require.

## SEC pipeline and public data

- `resolve-element`'s label-text fallback without a ticker now returns matches. The query was rejected every time and came back empty.
- Failed filings are retried on the nightly chain, and a retry reads the filer's full history when a filing is missing from the recent page.
- The public filing catalog lists every processed year, not just the ones held in the graph.
- xbrlkit moves to 0.20.4. Published filing artifacts follow one section-membership rule between the holon and the Tavi.

## Robustness

- Circuit breakers trip and close correctly. Graph API admission counters no longer drift, and the backup-download quota holds under parallel requests.
- Document search and password re-authentication run off the event loop. A test guard now fails any test in which platform async code blocks the loop.
- An uncached feature-flag read fails open on a network error, as intended.

## Security hardening

Document metadata parsing, GraphQL list resolution, MCP tool inputs and deploy-role scopes were
hardened.

## Documentation

- New product pages on security and your data, taking your data with you, and teams and roles.
- The console docs now cover the drawer, `/do` and the Activity page.
- Product videos are embedded across the product guides.
- The create-graph page describes RoboLedger and RoboInvestor in balance.
- The RoboSystems SEC connector is linked from Claude's connector directory.

## Housekeeping

- Release images publish to Docker Hub over OIDC, with no stored token, and the Python base image is pulled from the ECR Public mirror.
- Journey tests now run the platform's seams end to end against real Postgres and Valkey: subscription changes, the QuickBooks round trip, and a materialize killed mid-run.
- A `NOTICE` file carries the trademark attribution.
- Dependencies: oauthlib 4.0, pyjwt 2.15, urllib3 2.8.
